_readme: SAIRNlaw deadline engine -- holiday calendar extension, 2027 (amended) through 2031.
Phase 4 item 2. Loaded through add_holidays like every other calendar.
WHY THIS EXISTS: every jurisdiction carried 2026-2027 only, which was already
failing in production, not merely about to. A Pennsylvania matter triggered
2027-12-15 with a 60-day period crosses into 2028 and refused with
NOT_PROVISIONED -- verified live before this was built. The refusal was honest
and correct, but the coverage was going dark on 2028-01-01 regardless.
A REAL DEFECT IN THE PHASE 3 CALENDARS, found by the generator’s own
self-check rather than by a report: New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday,
so every both-way-shift jurisdiction (us-federal, in, mi, pa) observes it on
FRIDAY 2027-12-31. That date belongs to the 2027 calendar and was absent from
all four. Ohio is correctly unaffected -- O.R.C. 1.14 shifts Sunday only, so
its New Year’s Day 2028 stays on 2028-01-01, which is exactly the kind of
per-state divergence that would have been erased by generating one calendar
and copying it. The omission erred EARLY (a missing holiday means the engine
does not roll, producing a date earlier than the truth), which is the safe
direction, but it was real.
The 2027 rows here are the Phase 3 lists PLUS that one entry. They were not
regenerated -- those lists carry hand-verified reasoning in their authority
notes and re-deriving them would have discarded it.
Each jurisdiction’s shift rule is applied separately, never shared. The four
in this set genuinely differ, and that difference is load-bearing:
us-federal  Sat -> preceding Fri, Sun -> following Mon
oh          SUNDAY ONLY. No Saturday shift.
in          Sat -> preceding Fri, Sun -> following Mon
mi          five fixed days both ways; Christmas Eve / New Year’s Eve on a
FRIDAY shift BACKWARD to Thursday
pa          statutory dates do not shift; federal observed days added alongside
NOT EXTENDED, and deliberately so: Indiana municipal election days (vary by
locality), Pennsylvania county closure schedules (MCR-equivalent local
variance -- see that seed’s finding 5), and Michigan local administrative
orders. All three would require inventing facts about a specific court.

authority.note: AMENDED 2027. New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday, so this jurisdiction observes it on FRIDAY 2027-12-31 -- a date that belongs to the 2027 calendar, not 2028. That entry was MISSING from the Phase 3 calendars and is added here. Found by the calendar generator’s own self-check, not by a report: the engine resolves holidays by the year of the date, and the endpoint validator rejects a date whose year does not match its calendar, so the entry would have been silently unreachable if filed under 2028. Every other 2027 entry is the Phase 3 list unchanged. Both-way shift per IC 1-1-9-1(b). Includes Abraham Lincoln’s Birthday and Good Friday; EXCLUDES Juneteenth, which IC 1-1-9-1 does not list. Statewide election days are included in even years only, matching the 2026 encoding; municipal elections vary by locality and remain unenumerable.

authority.note: AMENDED 2027. New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday, so this jurisdiction observes it on FRIDAY 2027-12-31 -- a date that belongs to the 2027 calendar, not 2028. That entry was MISSING from the Phase 3 calendars and is added here. Found by the calendar generator’s own self-check, not by a report: the engine resolves holidays by the year of the date, and the endpoint validator rejects a date whose year does not match its calendar, so the entry would have been silently unreachable if filed under 2028. Every other 2027 entry is the Phase 3 list unchanged. Per MCR 8.110(D)(2)(b): the five fixed days shift Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday, while Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve shift BACKWARD to Thursday when they fall on a Friday and to Friday when they fall on a weekend. No Columbus Day. This remains the MCR default -- MCR 8.110(D)(2)(c) authorises local administrative orders modifying it.
